articles.title: 比亚迪第三代唐预扣提车价曝光：后驱激光尊荣型 22.5 万元，四季度上市
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 22 日消息，博主 @迪粉之家 今日曝光了一份关于比亚迪第三代唐的经销商预扣款：850km 后驱激光尊荣型预扣款 22.5 万元，850km 后驱激光旗舰型 24 万元。四驱版本尚未开启采购通道，正式售价仍需等待官方发布。IT之家注：预扣款是经销商向厂家打款的内部结算参考，不等于最终指导价，但通常与上市定价存在一定关联。比亚迪第三代唐定位纯电中大型 SUV，长宽高约为 5045/1980/1760mm，轴距 2950mm。其外观延续王朝系列最新设计语言，封闭式前脸搭配上扬大灯与贯穿镀铬饰条，车尾为贯穿灯组，BYD 标识嵌入灯带中央。内饰提供沙丘米与丹霞橙两种配色，座舱设计灵感来自科幻飞船操控台。前排头枕拆卸后可与后排坐垫拼接形成“大床模式”，面向户外休憩场景。车内采用一体式联屏，中控上方另有一块狭长辅助屏，用于显示多媒体、天气及挡位模式等信息。动力方面，单电机后驱版最大功率 300kW，电池提供 88.682kWh 与 105.792kWh 两种规格，CLTC 续航覆盖 730km、830km 与 850km 三个版本。底盘配置上，新车全系标配天神之眼 B 智驾系统与云辇-A 智能空气悬架，双腔空悬搭配路面预瞄功能，可根据路况实时调整悬架状态。相关阅读：《比亚迪第三代唐四驱版申报：双电机峰值功率 215、300 kW，四季度上市》《本季度上市：比亚迪第三代唐将首搭全新巨幕 UI 交互系统，还有 AI 萌宠桌面》《比亚迪公布第三代唐内饰：设计灵感来自“宇宙飞船控制台”》《比亚迪王朝 8 系旗舰之作：第三代唐 SUV 全球首秀，四季度上市》

articles.title: 北汽集团：与宁德时代签署合作协议，多品牌车型将接入巧克力换电
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 22 日消息，10 月 22 日，北京汽车集团有限公司（简称“北汽集团”）和宁德时代新能源科技股份有限公司（简称“宁德时代”）正式签署全面深化换电业务合作协议。北汽集团党委书记、董事长张建勇，宁德时代董事长兼 CEO 曾毓群出席签约仪式并见证签约。据介绍，双方将立足全链条深度协同，在整车与电池产品设计与研发、换电站网络建设、电池能源服务产品打造与推广、商业模式创新等领域全面深化合作；共同推动行业换电标准统一、网络互通共享、加速实现换电科技全民普惠；联手构筑成熟换电产业生态。北汽集团表示，公司将积极推进旗下多品牌适配车型接入宁德时代巧克力换电生态系统，依托双方集团级战略协同优势，共建覆盖全国、高效互通的公共补能基础设施。北汽集团与宁德时代将携手推动换电资产的专业化整合，以分工协作模式提升产业效率，推动换电标准加速统一。同时，北汽集团将开放经销商网络，宁德时代巧克力换电将围绕门店精准建站，与北汽经销商团队深度探索共建联营模式。北汽集团称，此次战略合作的签署，标志着中国新能源汽车换电赛道在标准统一、资产互通、资源共享上迈出关键一步。北汽集团与宁德时代以统一标准推动行业发展，以共享网络升级全民出行体验，共同助推中国新能源汽车产业高质量、可持续发展。

articles.title: 长春生产：消息称奥迪正在与华为谈判，共同开发新一代中国版 A8
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 22 日消息，当地时间 10 月 20 日，德国经理人杂志（简称《经理人》）大篇幅刊发了奥迪将与华为合作在中国生产下一代 A8 的消息，同时透露包括奥迪在中国油电销量双双遇阻、更换中国市场管理层、希望通过与华为合作重振奥迪一汽工厂等重磅信息。▲ 图源：华为乾崑智能汽车解决方案官网 | 全新奥迪 A6L《经理人》提到，现年 57 岁的奥迪股份公司全球 CEO 高德诺进行了一项用保时捷 Panamera 的 MSB 平台代替了 A8 最初的换代计划，并将于保时捷莱比锡工厂生产，而不是已经生产 A8 长达 34 年的奥迪内卡苏尔姆工厂。该计划在内部饱受争议。此外，高德诺还为中国定制了一个大胆的计划，而该计划甚至未先告知集团高层 —— A8 中国版车型将不再从德国出口，而是在中国直接生产，其核心研发源自华为。多位消息人士透露，中国版奥迪 A8 将获得华为的完整平台支持。上述方案目前未达成一致，据谈判圈内人士介绍，在华为架构上会有几款车型，最重要的是 A8，但还会有高端的一款 SUV。高德诺希望通过与华为的合作，振兴长春的 PPE 工厂，首批车在 2028 年底前生产出来。这么做背后的原因是奥迪的销量下降，预计奥迪 2026 年全球销量仅略高于 140 万辆，甚至可能低于 2011 年的销量。奥迪总部英戈尔施塔特表示，9 月底，奥迪已经收到了来自母公司大众集团财务总监严厉的盈利预警。另外，奥迪过去两年在中国的销量下滑还在可控范围内，但是 2026 年出现了危险的下滑趋势。据内部人士透露，预测 2026 年奥迪在中国的销量将仅高于 42 万辆，比 2025 年减少约 30%。这将是奥迪在中国市场 2012 年以来的最低销量。《经理人》还指出，在全球最赚钱的市场表现如此糟糕，以至于奥迪内部发出警告，或许迎来进入中国市场的第一次亏损。为此，奥迪中国或将换帅。而据IT之家今日早些时候报道，奥迪今日在全球官网宣布，自 2026 年 11 月 1 日起，中国区总裁将由张俊接任。这也是奥迪中国区迎来的首位中国籍总裁。

articles.title: 苹果已屏蔽 eMudhra 问题证书，防止攻击者伪造网站身份
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 22 日消息，IT之家昨日报道，印度证书颁发机构 eMudhra 的 8 个中间证书私钥被发现在生成时存在严重缺陷，Mozilla、谷歌、微软以及多个开发工具链已紧急吊销相关证书或发布更新。据 MacRumors 今日报道，苹果已于 10 月 19 日在旗下设备中屏蔽了存在安全问题的 eMudhra 中间证书，以防攻击者利用这些证书伪造网站身份。Mozilla 加密工程师 Dennis Jackson 于当地时间 10 月 20 日公布了相关事件的调查进展。根据 Mozilla 安全报告，受影响的是印度证书颁发机构 eMudhra 签发的 8 张中间证书，其私钥均存在生成缺陷。研究人员发现，这些密钥的数值均小于 256，因此只需简单尝试就能完成破解。中间证书用于建立网站证书的信任链。一旦攻击者掌握相关私钥，就可能签发冒充其他网站的证书。如果软件信任这些伪造证书，攻击者便可能冒充合法网站，并在能够拦截用户网络连接的情况下读取或篡改通信内容。Mozilla 表示，研究人员于 10 月 17 日报告了这一问题，Mozilla 随后通过 Firefox 的 OneCRL 机制屏蔽相关证书，无需用户更新或重启浏览器。谷歌也在同日通过 Chrome 的证书撤销列表屏蔽了 6 张受影响的 TLS 中间证书。苹果于 10 月 19 日采取了相应措施，微软则于 10 月 20 日跟进。eMudhra 在 10 月 20 日发布的声明中表示，公司已撤销受影响的证书，并正在调查事件原因。该公司称，受影响的中间证书中，只有一张曾部署于生产环境，且没有任何一张证书签发过面向终端用户的网站证书。相关阅读：《印度 eMudhra 中间证书私钥存在严重缺陷：Chrome、Firefox 迅速阻断，Go、Python、Rust 均需更新》

articles.content: IT之家 10 月 22 日消息，前 BioWare 高管 Mark Darrah 在自己的 YouTube 频道中表示，随着艺电宣布关闭 BioWare 工作室并终止《质量效应》新作的开发，公司未来出售《质量效应》《龙腾世纪》等游戏 IP 的可能性有所上升。不过，EA 也有可能选择将这些 IP 长期搁置，而非出售。BioWare 由 EA 100% 持有，《质量效应》《龙腾世纪》和《翡翠帝国》等游戏 IP 也归 EA 所有。工作室关闭并不会改变这些 IP 的所有权，但由于公司内部不再有团队负责开发相关游戏，EA 出售这些 IP 也在情理之中。Darrah 同时指出，EA 也可能选择将这些 IP 封存起来，不再继续开发。他认为，目前仍需等待一段时间，才能判断 EA 是否有意出售部分长期未开发的 IP。按照他的说法，EA 当前似乎仍处于控制成本的阶段，未来如果转向更积极的收入增长策略，出售 IP 或许会成为一个更具吸引力的选项。IT之家此前报道，EA 当地时间周三宣布关闭 BioWare。BioWare 随后确认工作室将结束运营，下一款《质量效应》游戏的早期开发工作也已停止。路透社报道称，此次调整属于 EA 缩减游戏开发项目、将资源集中于更具商业潜力作品的计划之一，公司预计裁减约 400 个岗位，其中约 50 个岗位来自 BioWare。《质量效应》系列上一部作品《质量效应：仙女座》于 2017 年推出。BioWare 此后于 2020 年公布正在开发该系列新作。与此同时，《龙腾世纪》系列最近一部作品《龙腾世纪：影障守护者》于 2024 年发布。相关阅读：《EA 启动成本削减计划：裁员 400 人、关闭 BioWare 工作室，并取消〈质量效应〉新作》

articles.title: 小鹏 IRON 人形机器人能力升级：每 0.2 秒重新推理一次，可预测 6 秒内动作变化
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 22 日消息，小鹏汽车今日宣布，上个月，第二代 VLA 开始理解“时间”；这个月，它来到小鹏 IRON 身上理解“你的下一步”。依赖同一个物理 AI 基座，第二代 VLA 大模型全新升级后，获得更强的时序理解与未来行为预测能力；这一能力也已端侧落地到小鹏人形机器人 IRON 上。据介绍，小鹏 IRON 与人握手、碰拳、击掌，还能灵活应对互动中的临时“变招”：手掌突然握拳，它随即调整回应；击掌位置改变，它也能换手配合。这些互动看似简单，难点却在于人不会按机器人的节奏出招。小鹏 IRON 不是识别一次手势、做完一套动作才反应，而是一直观察、实时判断、持续调整。它每 0.2 秒根据眼前画面重新推理一次，并预测 6 秒内的动作变化，让“看到什么”和“身体怎么动”连成实时闭环。IT之家注意到，小鹏于 2025 年 11 月 5 日举行的科技日活动上发布全新一代人形机器人 IRON，猫步走得像人一样。据官方介绍，小鹏全新一代人形机器人 IRON 猫步走得像人一样轻柔，还拥有像人一样思考“大脑”。IRON 作为最拟人的人形机器人，拥有「骨骼-肌肉-皮肤」：仿人脊椎、仿生肌肉、全包覆柔性皮肤、头部 3D 曲面显示、仿生灵动双肩、实现 22 个自由度的灵巧手。据IT之家了解，全新一代人形机器人 IRON 搭载物理世界大模型，拥有 3 颗图灵 AI 芯片，构建 VLT+VLA+VLM 高阶大小脑能力组合，可实现对话、行走、交互等高阶智能。根据计划，小鹏将在 2026 年底实现人形机器人量产，2027 年上半年开启交付，率先落地门店、商场等商业场景，并逐步拓展至工业及家庭场景。

articles.title: 商务部：截至 2025 年末，我国每个家庭平均拥有手机 2.5 部
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 22 日消息，国新办今日举行“开局起步‘十五五’”系列主题新闻发布会，介绍推进“十五五”时期商务高质量发展有关情况。会上介绍，我国居民消费正在由追求“量的满足”向“质的提升”转变。截至 2025 年末，我国每个家庭平均拥有手机 2.5 部、电视 1.1 台、冰箱 1.1 台、洗衣机 1 台。在“有没有”的问题已经解决后，大家自然更加关注“好不好”。一方面，消费者更加注重商品和服务的质量，“既要花得值、更要买得对”；另一方面，不同消费群体需求呈现多样化、个性化、差异化特点。绿色、智能、健康等消费需求不断释放。例如，从智能手机到智能穿戴，再到当前火爆的人形机器人和外骨骼机器人，各类智能产品正在逐步走进千家万户。图源：PexelsIT之家查询获悉，2026 年 1-9 月，国内市场手机出货量 1.89 亿部，其中，5G 手机 1.71 亿部，占同期手机出货量的 90.6%。2026 年 9 月，国内手机上市新机型 45 款，其中 5G 手机 33 款，同比增长 43.5%，占同期手机上市新机型数量的 73.3%。2026 年 1-9 月，国内手机上市新机型 286 款，同比下降 28.1%，其中 5G 手机 174 款，同比下降 3.3%，占同期手机上市新机型数量的 60.8%。

articles.title: Anthropic 平台工程团队全面采用 Claude 编码，工程师转向系统设计与验证
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 22 日消息，当地时间周二，Anthropic 平台工程团队负责人 Katelyn Lesse 在 Grafana Labs 举办的 ObservabilityCON 活动上透露，“就我们团队及我们的系统开发和维护工作而言，我们所有代码都是 Claude 写的，真的是全部。”该团队目前编写和维护系统所需的代码已全部由 Claude 生成，工程师的工作则更多集中在系统设计、验证和代码质量把关上。据介绍，团队已开始让 AI 智能体自主修复测试，并正在探索允许智能体直接修改代码库的方式。公开报道显示，Katelyn Lesse 主要负责 Anthropic 的平台工程团队，负责公司的核心服务、开发者工具和产品基础设施。据《商业内幕》报道，该团队今年夏季的员工人数约为 200 人。她表示，工程师仍然负责系统设计和验证工作，随后将实际编码任务交给 Claude。在一次大型代码库从 Python 迁移到 Rust 的过程中，团队成员设计了验证机制，以确认最终产物符合预期。至于代码组件的开发、监控以及验证过程中的大量具体工作，则由 AI 智能体完成。Lesse 还透露，Anthropic 已经允许 AI 智能体在没有人工干预的情况下自主修复测试。随着过去一年 AI 模型能力的提升，公司正在考虑如何逐步允许智能体直接修改实际代码库。她表示，工程管理人员对这一变化仍然十分谨慎，但允许智能体自主修改代码的界限正在发生变化。Anthropic 对 AI 编程工具的应用并不局限于平台工程团队。根据 Anthropic 于 2026 年 6 月发布的技术报告，截至当年 5 月，Claude 编写的代码占公司合并至生产代码库的代码行数的 80% 以上。Anthropic 于 10 月 16 日发布的另一份报告则显示，AI 智能体正在改变公司的工作组织和招聘结构。2025 年初至 2026 年期间，初级员工在公司技术部门中的占比从 21% 降至 14%，初级技术岗位在技术部门招聘中的占比则从 27% 降至 9%。Anthropic 表示，随着 AI 工具承担更多代码编写和漏洞排查工作，公司招聘人员时更加重视候选人的自主性与判断能力。相关阅读：《Anthropic 修订使用政策，首次禁止用户虐待 Claude AI 模型》《Anthropic 发布 Claude Sonnet 5.5：速度提升 30%，智能体编码性能反超 Opus 5.5》《Anthropic 发布 Claude Opus 5.5 模型：性能媲美 Fable 5.1，运行成本比 Opus 5 低 40%》《Anthropic 发布 Claude Fable 5.1 和 Mythos 5.1：性能超越前代，缓存降价 75%》

articles.content: IT之家 10 月 22 日消息，据南宁轨道交通官方通报，2026 年 10 月 22 日 9 时 30 分，南宁轨道交通 1 号线东盟商务区站下行 11205 次列车车厢内发生乘客随身携带的充电宝自燃冒烟的情况。本次事件未造成人员受伤、未造成设备损坏及线路运营延误，全线网运营秩序平稳正常。IT之家附南宁轨道交通情况说明原文如下：情况说明2026 年 10 月 22 日 9 时 30 分，南宁轨道交通 1 号线东盟商务区站下行 11205 次列车车厢内发生乘客随身携带的充电宝自燃冒烟的情况。事件发生后，车站工作人员第一时间响应，迅速开展列车清客、隐患排查等现场处置工作，将该充电宝移至站台安全区域进行处置，现场风险已完全排除。本次事件未造成人员受伤、未造成设备损坏及线路运营延误，全线网运营秩序平稳正常。南宁轨道交通温馨提醒广大乘客：乘坐地铁时，请妥善保管好随身携带的电子产品，如遇设备发热、冒烟等异常情况，请第一时间告知工作人员，共同维护轨道交通出行安全。据新京报今日报道，南宁地铁 1 号线一列车行至东盟商务区站时旅客携带物品起火，车站工作人员使用水基型灭火器将火扑灭，并将起火物品转移至站台。

articles.title: “卡比之父”樱井政博：AI 催生大量模仿游戏，真正具备创造力的开发者将变得更加重要
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 22 日消息，据游戏媒体 VGC 今天报道，被誉为“卡比之父”的游戏开发者樱井政博最近看到了一组数据：2010 年他创立游戏设计者奖时，Steam 每年新增游戏约为 275 款；如今日本市场新增游戏数量已接近 1.9 万款。IT之家注意到，樱井政博对此表示，AI 日益普及将催生大量克隆游戏和模仿作品，游戏数量还会继续增长。但这些游戏大多数都难以在商业上成功，因为它们只是在模仿已有作品。他认为，随着 AI 复制游戏创意的能力越来越强，真正具备创造力的开发者，将变得越来越重要。他对此解释称：“假设 AI 有一天能够制作各种各样的游戏。例如它能够学习上田文人，制作出类似《古堡迷踪》《汪达与巨像》的游戏。但现实是，AI 无法制作出上田文人未来要开发的作品，只有他自己能够决定未来游戏的艺术方向，这恰恰体现了人类独有的‘原创性’。”

articles.title: Show HN: Return Ledger free portfolio TWR/XIRR tracker with AI PDF import
articles.content: Hi HN, I made a simple single-page tool that computes portfolios return / performance (TWR and XIRR), gross and net of fees and tax. It requires logging all transactions. It's client-side, with no accounts, and data lives in the browser localStorage.It started as a personal tool . I wanted a way to understand what was the return of my portfolio and of a tenanted rental property (XIRR).The experimental part is an import: you upload a broker's trade notice PDF and an LLM proposes one ledger row, which you confirm. It solves a problem I had: understanding my bank's documents, especially for bonds, at least here in Italy, where there are multiple numbers to add or subtract to get the real return.It's an alpha. I've only tested it on real documents from one Italian bank (about 40 notices, all correct on the first attempt) and on a few synthetic ones from other countries, so I'd really like to hear how it does on yours.Caveats: the PDF goes to the model provider and is neither stored nor log

articles.title: 2026 世界顶尖科学家论坛 10 月 30 日开幕，33 位顶尖奖项得主确认参会
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 22 日消息，2026 世界顶尖科学家论坛将于 10 月 30 日至 11 月 1 日在上海临港中心 —— 世界顶尖科学家论坛永久会址举办，开幕式暨主论坛定于 10 月 31 日上午举行。本届论坛将汇聚 33 位诺贝尔奖、图灵奖、沃尔夫奖、菲尔兹奖等国际顶级奖项得主，众多海内外院士、知名专家学者、优秀青年科学家代表，以及科创龙头企业代表等，聚焦全球科技前沿，共同探讨基于未来科学的科研范式。本届论坛以“范式变革：科学突破的下一个十年”为主题，论坛由中国科协主办，深圳市鹏瑞公益基金会、红杉慈善基金会联合主办，另有 25 家国际、国内科学组织及一流高校、顶尖实验室参与承办和支持，中国科协原主席万钢与 2013 年诺贝尔生理学或医学奖得主兰迪 · 谢克曼共同担任大会主席。本届论坛的总体架构为“1+6+4+1”，即 1 场开幕式暨主论坛、6 场平行论坛、4 场主题活动和 1 场闭幕式，并配套科技参访、顶科校园行等衍生活动。截至目前，已确认参会的顶尖科学家共 33 位，其中诺贝尔奖得主 7 位、图灵奖得主 3 位，7 位为首次参会；另有资深科学家 139 位、青年科学家 81 位，首次参会占比均超过 80%。华人高层次学者与两院院士的参会规模较往届显著提升。开幕式上将颁发 2026 世界顶尖科学家奖。IT之家此前报道，该奖已于 9 月 10 日公布获奖名单，共 11 位科学家分获“智能科学或数学奖”“生命科学或医学奖”和今年增设的“青年科学家奖”。北京生命科学研究所邵峰成为该奖创设以来首位中国籍获奖者，他与袁钧瑛、王晓东及美国基因泰克公司的维什瓦 · 迪克西特共同获得“生命科学或医学奖”，表彰他们阐明不同形式程序性细胞死亡的分子通路。主论坛的主旨演讲阵容体现了本届论坛对“基础科学与产业需求对话”的侧重。2025 年诺贝尔化学奖得主奥马尔 · 亚吉、中国科学院院士胡海岚、2002 年菲尔兹奖得主洛朗 · 拉福格与宁德时代创始人、董事长曾毓群将先后发表演讲。据发布会介绍，这是产业领域领军科学家代表首次与顶尖奖项得主围绕论坛核心议题同台交流。奥马尔 · 亚吉将提出“选择科学”概念，探讨借助人工智能筛选高价值研究方向；胡海岚将围绕抑郁症发病机制与氯胺酮快速抗抑郁原理展开分享；洛朗 · 拉福格则从思想与文化视角讨论大模型。智谱 AI 创始人唐杰、寒武纪创始人陈云霁等科学家型企业家也将参会。六场平行论坛分别聚焦未来半导体、人工智能、生物医药、空天信息、未来能源与量子科学，由上海大学、华东师范大学、临港国家实验室、上海交通大学、复旦大学、同济大学分别承办。与往届相比，平行论坛的定位更明确地指向成果转化：生物医药论坛聚焦阿尔茨海默病、帕金森病与抑郁症三大中枢神经疾病，组织科研、临床与投资方跨界对话；未来能源论坛试图凝练“值得落地”的问题，打通从论文到中试的接口；空天信息论坛则紧扣商业航天从“技术验证”向“规模化运营”过渡的阶段特征。论坛还首次成立中外联合学术委员会，由上海市科协主席张杰院士与美国纽约科学院院长杜宁凯院士分任中外方主任，15 位科学家对议题设置、议程安排与嘉宾遴选实行全流程把关；六大领域平行论坛共收到论文投稿 132 篇。相关阅读：《2026 世界顶尖科学家奖在沪揭晓：华人科学家首获顶科奖，邵峰成首位中国籍得主》

articles.title: 古尔曼：苹果正测试第二代 iPhone Duo 原型机，配备面容 ID
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 22 日消息，彭博社记者马克 · 古尔曼最近透露，苹果内部正在测试的第二代 iPhone Duo 原型机已配备面容 ID，其面部识别传感器集成在外屏下方。iPhone Duo 没有使用面容 ID，是许多首批上手者最诟病的地方之一。对苹果来说，如何将完整面容 ID 组件塞入折叠屏手机薄薄的机身，绝对是重大课题。并且这家公司一直在努力缩小面容 ID 的体积，降低其对屏幕设计的影响，iPhone 18 Pro 的红外摄像头就是最好例子。随着 iPhone Duo 2 和二十周年纪念版 iPhone 即将推出，苹果可能进一步改进面容 ID，将红外摄像头和泛光感应元件都隐藏在屏幕下方，进一步缩小屏幕开孔面积。如果相关进展顺利，第二代 iPhone Duo 面世时可能会搭载面容 ID；但如果研发进度延迟，我们可能得等到 iPhone Duo 3 才能见到。IT之家注意到，古尔曼还透露，苹果员工一直试图将操作按钮加入下一代 iPhone Duo，能否实现尚不确定。

articles.content:
arXiv:2610.26942v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Automated theorem provers often rely on sampling language models, but proof assistants like Lean reject each failed step with a precise error message --- information that pure sampling discards. To overcome this, we introduce a bounded, online step-level repair module. Our search samples $K$ candidate tactics at each step and repairs a failed tactic at most $R$ times. Instead of discarding failed tactics, we feed the compiler's error message to a pretrained repair model to fix individual rejected steps in place. This approach improves the solve rate over a sampling-only baseline across all tested candidate budgets ($K \in \{1,3,5,8\}$), achieving up to a $32\%$ relative gain and solving $82$ additional theorems on a $1{,}990$-theorem subset of the LeanDojo benchmark. articles.title: SPEM: Structure-Aware Procedural Memory for Efficient Skill Use in LLM Agents
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.26995v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM-based agents increasingly rely on reusable skills. However, scaling skill libraries makes efficient and accurate skill use difficult. Full skill loading incurs high token and runtime overhead. In contrast, flat semantic retrieval treats skills as independent text entries, ignoring dependencies, execution order, state transitions, and data flow constraints. We propose SPEM, a lightweight structure-aware procedural memory framework for efficient skill use in LLM-based agents. SPEM maintains Atomic Skill Memory for individual skills and Skill-DAG Memory for reusable compositions derived from successful executions. For a new task, SPEM reuses high-confidence Skill-DAG templates when available. Otherwise, it retrieves atomic skills and invokes Skill-GNN for state- and structure-aware skill selection. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.27027v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Multi-agent LLM systems improve performance on clinical tasks, and that improvement is often read as evidence of a more trustworthy system. However, the two are not the same claim. A clinician acts on the stated reasoning and not only on the conclusion, so whether collaboration reduces hallucination, and what decides when it does, has to be measured in the reasoning too. Yet most evaluations score only the final answer. We evaluate four systems (a single-LLM baseline and three multi-agent topologies) across four models and three clinical tasks, scoring hallucination, under a factuality and faithfulness taxonomy, inside the rationale each system generates and reporting it alongside the task metric. We report that collaboration buys task performance but not lower hallucination as a rule, and no topology is reliably better than another. articles.content:

Abstract: In recent years, physical artificial intelligence (physical AI) has experienced rapid development, capturing significant attention in academia and industry. However, the field has yet to reach consensus on its definition, technical landscape, and core challenges. To address this gap, this monograph seeks to define physical AI, present its technical landscape, and examine each key technical subfield in depth. In doing so, it establishes a unified framework for Physical AI: artificial systems that perceive, model, and act upon the physical world through continuous feedback under real-world constraints. Further, this monograph distinguishes physical AI from conventional digital AI, embodied AI, cyber-physical systems, and digital twins. Abstract: Recent Omni LLMs (OLLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in joint audio-visual reasoning, yet cross-modal hallucinations remain a major challenge. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.27115v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM agents act on the external world through tools and third-party skills, so a single executed action can cause irreversible harm. Existing defenses judge a proposed action without tracking whether its content comes from the user or from external sources such as tool outputs, and they judge it in isolation rather than against an available alternative, which forces a trade-off between security and utility. We present PROVISO, a controller that decides which action to commit after the agent proposes an action and before it is executed. PROVISO encodes trusted observations, external observations, the proposed action, and an alternative into provenance-typed memory, relates them through role-specific queries, and commits the action with the highest calibrated value learned from outcomes. Abstract: LLM agents perform tasks over multiple steps and revise their actions based on feedback. As the total reasoning budget is often limited and must support future steps, the agent must choose between short and long reasoning before each action. Longer reasoning may improve the final task outcome by preventing later errors, but it also uses budget capacity that may be needed for future decisions. This creates two challenges: estimating the downstream value of long reasoning and deciding when that value is worth using the remaining budget. We propose Paired Outcome-guided Reasoning Allocation (PORA), which learns this decision by comparing short and long reasoning from the same interaction state. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28707v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: When training LLMs to code with reinforcement learning, reward hacking is often detectable but difficult to prevent, since (a) environment hardening is increasingly difficult as training environments grow more complex; and (b) training-time interventions incentivize models to obfuscate hacking behavior to bypass detection.
  We instead study whether we can predict when detectable reward hacking becomes dominant before executing an RL run, enabling us to select lower-risk recipes in advance. We find that the initial hacking rate alone does not determine onset, which varies substantially across training recipes and repeated runs. We thus formulate this problem as predicting the distribution of the reward hacking onset step under a target training recipe.

Abstract: Evaluating the energy transmission ratio of an X-ray beam through a polymer composite is a challenging task in radiation shielding studies. The reference solution with Monte Carlo transport simulation is highly accurate but computationally expensive: each of our reference simulations is capped at $4\times10^9$ photon histories and a 20,000 s (over 5 hours) time limit, while closed-form analytical methods fail to represent such complex scenarios. The model is a Set Transformer, which makes it permutation invariant by construction and accepts mixtures of different sizes up to 11 constituents within a fixed-size padded set. Abstract: LLM-based methods for node classification on text-attributed graphs (TAGs) routinely report state-of-the-art accuracy. We ask how these results compare with inexpensive baselines run on the same splits. On the splits of three recent studies, we tune four baseline representatives with validation-only selection and compare them with the highest mean that each paper reports for an LLM-based method in the matched setting. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28770v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: RLVR improves language-model reasoning, but commonly relies on independent stochastic rollouts for exploration, which can repeatedly sample similar failed strategies. Prior work has seen success with approaches that guide exploration by introducing dependence into the sampling process by including incorrect solutions in the context for subsequent attempts. Still, these methods introduce the additional question of how to assign credit to each attempt. We propose to view the credit assignment through the lens of Stochastic Shortest Paths, a framework in classical reinforcement learning that seeks to minimize the expected cumulative cost to reach a terminal state (in our case, a verified successful response). We show that, under suitable simplifying assumptions, this perspective naturally leads to a simple modification to GRPO, which we call Retry-Aware Policy Optimization (ReAPO). articles.title: Motion Equivariant Convolutional LSTM: When Motion Becomes a Gauge Symmetry
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28771v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Objects move, cameras pan, and weather drifts with the wind: much of what changes in sequential data is motion. Motion changes where things are, not what they are, and is therefore a symmetry of the data. Yet standard recurrent networks are not equivariant to it: their memory stays put while the input moves on. Flow equivariant recurrent networks first brought this symmetry into sequence models, for motions of constant velocity, or flows, by enumerating a bank of velocities. We extend this idea in three directions: from simple recurrent networks to convolutional LSTMs, from flows to motions whose velocity changes in time, and from enumerating velocities to estimating them. Treating a sequence as a field over time, we show that motion becomes a gauge symmetry: a global symmetry made local in time. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28773v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Non-uniform allocation can improve post-training pruning of large language models, yet quality can still degrade sharply at high sparsity. To control degradation as sparsity increases, we introduce LADDER (Layer-Wise Allocation via Damage-Driven Evaluation and Refinement), which allocates sparsity incrementally. At each step, it evaluates pruning an additional fraction of weights from each eligible layer and commits the layer update that causes the least end-to-end degradation per removed parameter. This process produces non-uniform sparsity profiles and exactly nested masks across multiple budgets. We evaluate LADDER on five OPT, Llama, and Qwen models across 10-90% sparsity, using SparseGPT as its candidate-generation backend and comparing against uniform and adaptive allocation baselines. articles.title: Second Thoughts: Exploring and Planning through Comparative Imagination in World Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28779v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: World models let agents compare imagined outcomes before acting, but an agent must still decide which alternatives to explore and when a proposed plan should replace its learned policy. We introduce SDI (Sibling Disagreement in Imagination), which connects these decisions through a shared actor-based reference. SDI compares action sequences imagined from the same model state, using repeated rollouts of the actor's own sequence to measure variation under fixed behavior. This reference scales both the spread across candidate returns, which provides an exploration signal, and a proposed plan's predicted advantage, which governs action acceptance. The agent executes a planned action when its advantage exceeds the reference variability by a fixed factor; otherwise, it follows the actor. Abstract: Aggressive low-state weight quantization can substantially reduce neural-network representational flexibility, making predictive performance difficult to preserve when only a few discrete weight states are available. We investigate this regime for Transformer-based electricity-load forecasting using 3-, 5-, 7-, and 16-state weight quantization across feed-forward-only and attention-plus-feed-forward quantization. articles.content:

Abstract: Training tool-using language models requires costly interaction, yet identical rewards within a rollout group provide no group-relative learning signal. We use reward disagreement to guide harness evaluation and the allocation of rollouts for policy training in Model Context Protocol (MCP) environments. We first introduce Discord, which tests harness edits using exact paired inference and decision-preserving early stopping: only disagreeing paired outcomes favor one harness over another. This insight motivates prospective allocation in BRACE (Bank-calibrated Rollout Allocation under Correlated Episodes). BRACE combines historical task evidence, uncertainty in task success rates, and a correlated reward model to forecast mixed-reward groups before allocating generation budget. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28788v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Flow-matching policies adjust inference cost through the number of solver steps, but reinforcement learning at a single fixed solver budget can hide degradation at cheaper deployment budgets and even erase useful one-step behavior present in a pretrained policy. We introduce Action-Ratio-Clip Flow (ArcFlow), a deployment-aware algorithm for training one flow policy across a specified range of solver budgets. ArcFlow combines action-aligned supervision, budget exposure, and worst-budget checkpoint selection. For reconstruction objectives, its bridge aggregates temporal probes into one surrogate ratio and one PPO-style clip per action, with a boundary residual exactly equal to deployed one-step reconstruction error. Cycling exposes the shared field to the deployment range, and selection optimizes its performance floor. articles.title: CALLIOPE: Private Insights into AI Use, Without Embeddings
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28797v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We introduce CALLIOPE, a top-down framework for discovering topic hierarchies in large corpora of unstructured data (e.g., LLM conversations), while supporting differential privacy (DP). Unlike traditional and even recent LLM-augmented approaches that ultimately rely on clustering vector embeddings, our framework leverages LLM capabilities directly for the entire pipeline. Experiments demonstrate that this approach provides better utility over existing (embedding-based) methods in the DP setting, especially in the high privacy regime. We evaluate the quality of CALLIOPE outputs using a variety of traditionally studied clustering metrics, as well as some novel utility metrics that we introduce.

articles.title: An Explicit Feedback Contract for Iterative ML-Agent Harnesses
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28798v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Iterative ML agents develop models by editing code, running experiments, reading a validation score, and choosing what to try next. In current harnesses this loop is served by an exact validation score returned after every attempt, which leaves the validation split open to adaptive selection. In this work, we introduce an explicit feedback contract for ML-agent harnesses, which specifies what an agent may observe, when iteration should stop, and when the test split may be touched. The contract releases a validation score only when a submission clears a noise threshold computed from the paired standard error, so no margin has to be tuned. We ran experiments on click-through-rate prediction, learning to rank, and a control task with no signal to find. Abstract: While statistical learning has made remarkable progress in recent decades, driven by large datasets and data-driven protocols that have transformed scientific practice, it still faces a key limitation: it struggles to generalize beyond the data it has seen, often failing under distribution shift. Causality offers a promising solution: causal models focus on the underlying mechanisms of change rather than surface-level associations, enabling robust reasoning under external interventions. This allows systems not only to learn from data, but also to reason about hypothetical scenarios, adapt to new environments, and inform better decisions. Abstract: Agentic systems have demonstrated strong capabilities on complex tasks by enabling multiple interacting large language model (LLM)-based agents to collaborate and execute subtasks in parallel. However, this collaborative structure introduces new challenges for reliably evaluating and diagnosing system failures, particularly failure attribution: tracing a system's execution to identify the agent step responsible for an incorrect final outcome. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28849v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Latent diffusion models almost universally place a Gaussian prior on the VAE latent space. For base generation this default is unproblematic; under reinforcement-learning fine-tuning, however, it carries a structural limitation. The standard VAE's KL term does not merely ignore mode structure - it actively taxes separation and tightness. When data are multimodal, the ELBO optimum compresses distinct modes into an overlapping latent. RL fine-tuning amplifies this overlap: the score network is under-resolved on the saddle region between modes, dynamic-to-variational amplification rises sharply, and the collapse boundary beta_c is pushed far above its variational scale. On the real alanine-dipeptide Boltzmann distribution, a Gaussian-prior VAE collapses at beta_c = 0.224 while a mode-tracked Gaussian-mixture prior collapses at 0.00316, a 71x gap from the same pipeline.

articles.title: Translation and data ethics
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28710v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This chapter introduces data ethics for translation and discusses a number of ethical issues regarding data. These include issues of copyright, ownership and bias, which apply to all types of data, whereas there are further issues particular to minoritised language communities and those on either side of the digital divide, as data is implicated in power imbalances and dynamics. We close with a discussion of responsibility and regulation, and reflect on the growing attention on data ethics from translation studies researchers.

Abstract: Current evaluation of LLMs on benchmarks typically aggregates performance over individual examples into a single scalar score. articles.content:

Abstract: Evaluations of large language model (LLM) agents report that pricing agents collude at others' expense. Yet collusion is defined by enforcement: a cartel, in which competitors share monopoly profits, holds only if a member who cheats is punished. We introduce an audit that tests enforcement by forcing a member to cheat in counterfactual copies of a market, and use it to study what reinforcement learning (RL) teaches agents in pricing and trading. Small LLMs trained by RL learn what their training rivals reward, but only what they readily try. Abstract: Common instruction following (IF) benchmarks, such as IFEval, evaluate the ability of language models (LMs) to follow simple constraints that can easily be verified programmatically. Constraints are scoped to certain document sections, providing finer control over constraint density. Abstract: Dependency parsing resource development for Arabic has largely focused on Modern Standard Arabic, leaving dialectal Arabic comparatively under-resourced. We introduce MADARTB, the first large-scale parallel dependency treebank spanning five city dialects: Beirut, Cairo, Doha, Rabat and Tunis, and extending an existing parallel MSA version. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28838v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: High-quality human-translated parallel corpora can improve cross-lingual transfer, but are typically too small for large-scale pretraining. Machine-translated web corpora help overcome this limitation, making parallel data available at pretraining scale. We investigate how to use the parallel structure of the data to improve multilingual pretraining by concatenating each document with its translation in the same training sequence. We compare this parallel pretraining (PPT) approach with standard pretraining (SPT), training models from scratch at matched token budgets. Abstract: Early-grade reading screening is critical for identifying children at risk of reading difficulty. Existing AI-based screeners are often limited in the scope of their analyses and evaluation metrics, or are proprietary systems that lack transparent model specifications and evaluation. We adapt pretrained word and phoneme recognizers to children's speech, reducing word error rate from 13.88% to 8.84% and phoneme error rate from 41.66% to 23.00%. Powered by these child-adapted models, we implement Word Reading (WRE) and Oral Reading Fluency (ORF), two foundational tasks in K-2 screening. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28886v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM judges increasingly mediate benchmark evaluation, model selection, data curation, and training. Their decisions are useful only when each judge responds reliably to changes affecting its scoring criterion. Existing methods for reliability testing perturb inputs with known expected effects on judge scores. Prominent LLM-judge testing harnesses combine human-authored perturbation recipes with synthetic test generation, leaving scorer-specific recipe ideation outside the automated pipeline. This limits their use to fixed perturbations and pre-assumed scorer types. We introduce SANE, an agent-based framework that encodes behavioral requirements for stochastic evaluators as reusable agent instructions. Given a scorer specification, implementation, and representative inputs, the pipeline first identifies scorer-specific capabilities, then automatically derives perturbation recipes and expected score relations for each. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28887v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Autonomous agents can increasingly propose ideas, modify code, and run experiments, creating an opportunity to accelerate scientific discovery using teams of collaborative AI researchers. To escape local minima in the discovery, we propose to encourage orthogonal exploration by constructing the team using agents with varying expertise. However, realizing this design requires more than diverse backgrounds. When experiments are costly, a team can test only a limited number of ideas, thereby creating the need to balance exploration and exploitation when selecting a subset of researchers to propose and execute new experiments. Furthermore, each result should shape what the team tries next. We therefore ask how AI researchers with different scientific backgrounds can build on one another's findings and sustain progress under a limited experimental budget. Abstract: Cross-tokenizer logits distillation enables knowledge transfer across model families, allowing students to learn from stronger or more specialized teachers. However, differences in vocabulary and segmentation make teacher and student next-token distributions difficult to align. Existing logits-based methods are easy to integrate into standard distillation pipelines, but often rely on restrictive heuristics or tokenizer-pair-specific choices. They may restrict supervision to shared vocabulary subsets, require manually selecting different objectives for different tokenizer pairs, or match only the observed chunk and its complement rather than individual alternative continuations. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28944v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Semantic leakage occurs when a concept in the prompt steers model generation about an entity, even though the concept is irrelevant to it (e.g., a person who likes yellow is said to work as a school bus driver). It has mostly been studied in settings where the concept is directly attributed to the entity the model is asked about. This leaves open whether leakage is a flawed heuristic, where the model builds a profile of that entity, or a much broader associative tendency, e.g., working across seemingly unrelated entities. We argue for the latter: even after removing the attribution of the concept to the specific entity, leakage persists. Next, we extend this idea to gender bias. Abstract: Scanning every passage in a long document seems thorough, but does it preserve more useful evidence or produce better answers? We compare 11 retrieval configurations spanning lexical and dense search, hybrid reranking, and full-document scanning with Jev, OpenAI Decisions, and Cloudflare Clef. Full scans examine every passage initially, yet later reduction steps can discard relevant evidence. Abstract: Although large language models (LLMs) encode language in highly distributed spaces, they remain vulnerable to focal disruptions---a phenomenon strikingly similar to how localized brain damage causes clinical aphasia in humans. Abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates large language models by verifying drafted tokens in parallel. New draft-training objectives are usually credited with the acceptance they add over cross-entropy on externally written responses, yet many pipelines let the target rewrite them. Distillation and the gate add large gains on external responses, but after greedy regeneration, distillation adds a smaller gain and the gate little or none. Abstract: The development of face recognition has been strongly supported by the availability of large-scale training datasets. Among them, MS-Celeb-1M has played an important role by providing millions of facial images from nearly 100K identities. However, the size and heterogeneity of such datasets increase the likelihood of annotation errors, redundant samples, and other forms of data inconsistency. This motivated the introduction of refined versions, such as MS1MV2 and MS1MV3, aimed at improving the quality of the training data. Abstract: Conventional surgical segmentation relies on closed-set categories or explicit text queries, which cannot resolve implicit queries that require reasoning about workflows, instrument functions, and temporal relationships. Abstract: Most unified multimodal models treat images and text asymmetrically: a pretrained language model generates text, an attached diffusion head generates images, and outputs that contain both are produced in a fixed order, so the first output cannot adapt to the second. We ask whether both modalities can instead be generated by one process that is trained on them jointly from scratch. We therefore model the joint distribution directly in these spaces. Abstract: In vision and scientific domains involving spatial data, a key question is whether node feature values vary independently across space or form coherent spatial structures. Classical spatial autocorrelation statistics such as Moran's $I$ and Geary's $C$ quantify this phenomenon but operate on a single scalar variable with fixed neighbourhood weights, limiting their use for high-dimensional graph-like data. Existing registration methods are typically tailored to a single domain, with carefully tuned architectures and hyperparameters, and thus degrade markedly when applied to novel domains. Abstract: Conventional visual sensing faces a fundamental dilemma: information that should remain private today may need to be recovered tomorrow. Abstract: Clothes-Changing Person Re-Identification (CC-ReID) remains challenging due to drastic appearance shifts across outfits. Most prior works devise biometric signal-extraction heuristics to enhance inter-person variance, e.g., using segmentation masks, while leaving intra-person variance uncontrolled. We present MINER, a simple model-agnostic framework that suppresses garment bias by contrasting hard examples and adaptively balancing dataset-dependent intra- and inter-person variance. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28954v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Coarse-to-real (C2R) video generation converts coarse animation, simulation, or game-rendered videos into photorealistic videos while preserving scene layout, camera motion, and dynamics. Training such models requires aligned (coarse, realistic) video pairs, which are expensive to create and confine prior systems to narrow synthetic domains. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28962v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Accurate 6-DoF object pose tracking is essential for robotic interaction, yet conventional monocular pipelines frequently suffer from catastrophic divergence under rapid object motion. We present RoPT, a robust tracking framework engineered to overcome this limitation by unifying visual perception, temporal kinematics, and global re-localization into a tightly coupled closed loop. Unlike existing open-loop trackers, RoPT delivers three critical capabilities that fundamentally alter system resilience. First, the visual perception component tracks object masks to robustly handle partial and severe occlusions. Second, a kinematic factor graph regularizes frame-to-frame updates, forecasts forward pose predictions, and drives a parallel multi-hypothesis verification scheme to bypass local minima. Abstract: The scarcity of large annotated datasets limits deep learning (DL) segmentation in material CT analysis. DL-based pseudo-labeling can help, but it is often computationally expensive and hard to interpret. We introduce a multi-stage, model-free framework that generates pseudo-labels directly from grayscale CT scans. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.29003v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Text-to-image (T2I) platforms typically return several images per prompt so users can explore different visual interpretations and choose one that matches their intent. However, T2I models are usually optimized for single-image quality which comes at a cost of multi-image diversity, limiting this exploration. Diversity is also contextual: one user wants variations in background, while another wants them in artistic style, and the same user may later want variations in clothing. The generated images should differ along whatever axis the user cares about. In this paper, we introduce T-DIG, a text-conditioned diversity framework for image generation and editing. Abstract: In recent years, automated fruit classification systems have become a more critical component in precision agriculture for efficient yield estimation, quality control, and supply chain optimization. However, they still face significant challenges under varying quality, fruit maturity, illumination, texture degradation, morphological attributes, domain shift, and post-harvest handling conditions. This is a real-world setting where models that have been trained on specific quality grades must generalize to unseen grades to handle significant domain shift. articles.title: Real-Time Ground Normal Vector Estimation for Spherical Mobile 3D Mapping using LiDAR-Inertial Odometry
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28701v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Accurate ground plane normal estimation is essential for odometry in spherical mobile mapping systems (SMMS), which face challenges from rapid rotations and limited ground coverage. We propose two RANSAC-based approaches: single-scan estimation with normal vector scoring and multi-step validation, and LiDAR-inertial odometry (LIO)-based estimation using a global 3D map. Evaluated across diverse real-world datasets against terrestrial laser scanner ground truth, results show that LIO-based estimation significantly outperforms single-scan methods in accuracy and robustness. Integrating ground normal estimates into the motion model improves pose estimation, supporting autonomous navigation in challenging and hazardous environments.

articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28761v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In human-robot interaction (HRI) tasks, humans may interact with the robot in either an active guiding or passive following state, resulting in distinct control objectives for each interaction mode. Most existing approaches rely on predefined switching thresholds to distinguish interaction modes, but their performance can be sensitive to measurement noise. To address this limitation, we propose a novel framework with the following key contributions. First, a neural network (NN) trained via meta-learning is developed to recognize human intention without manually defined thresholds. By successfully incorporating force-dependent parameters from the controller, the recognition rates are improved from 90.1\% to 99.1\% for the passive mode and from 79.8\% to 97.1\% for the active mode. Abstract: This paper presents a novel framework integrating a robust wrench observer with a hybrid pose and force controller for physical Human-Robot Interaction (pHRI). In pHRI tasks, robots are expected to perform task-space motions robustly while remaining compliance with human disturbance, which proposes distinct control objectives. Most existing approaches focus mainly on either robustness or compliance and rely on force sensors for real-time tracking. To address these limitations, we propose a novel framework with the following key contributions. Firstly, a neural network (NN) is trained to improve the observer performance by compensating for system friction and unmodeled dynamics. Secondly, a task-null-space decomposition is applied to separate the joint velocity and reduce the effect of the human disturbance on the observer. Abstract: Target-based extrinsic calibration estimates the rigid transform between sensors from a few observations of a known target, and its result is commonly assessed by the root-mean-square error of the fitted residuals. However, this scalar error is computed on the same observations and therefore cannot indicate whether to accept the result, re-extract, recollect or add observations. This paper presents VeriCalib, which formulates extrinsic calibration as a verifiable estimation problem and reports a calibration state. The key insight is a two-level extrinsic compensation mechanism, in which the extrinsic compensates the rigid part of each observation error at the residual level, and rotation and translation compensate each other at the parameter level. articles.content:

Abstract: In contact-rich manipulation, contact conditions can change before a visual policy updates its action plan. Recomputing the plan through the visual policy adds latency, while tactile feedback alone does not specify how the ongoing motion should be revised for the task. We introduce T-WLA, a world-language-action architecture that uses shared visual memory to guide both action generation and tactile correction. At each visual update, the visual branch integrates the current image, task instruction, and retrieved history into a visual memory that conditions base-action generation. The same memory is cached for a lightweight tactile editor, which combines it with the active action chunk and incoming touch to predict residual corrections to unexecuted actions without rerunning the visual branch. Abstract: Human video scales easily and does not need robot hardware, but existing methods require depth sensing, overlay the robot onto 2D video, or generate data only for the demonstrated objects. We present Real2Sem2Real (R2Sem2R), a real-to-semantic-to-real pipeline that turns one monocular RGB video of a human demonstration into thousands of robot demonstrations across the semantic object instances of a category. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28882v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Long-horizon robotic operation requires memory that scales with essential information rather than execution time. We present a parameter-space memory framework where each episode is stored as a separable object. A neural implicit representation is fitted to episode video from a shared, meta-learned initialization; the resulting weight delta constitutes the memory. Crucially, this delta remains a fixed size regardless of whether the episode spans a hundred or a hundred thousand frames. A learned projector maps the weight delta into token embeddings, conditioning a language model for question answering and a decoder for joint command regression, without frame retrieval at query time. On RoboMME, the language model exceeds chance across all question types, and the decoder achieves a mean $R^2$ of 0.51. Abstract: Trajectory demonstrations show robots how to behave but not why, leaving them to guess which features of the task actually matter. Incorrect guesses produce misaligned internal representations and lead to incorrect robot behaviors. Because task features are often semantically defined, we argue that natural language is better suited for specifying features rather than relying on demonstrations. Although existing representation editing methods have proposed using language to specify new features, only allowing additive edits produces feature sets that are often over-specified or too narrowly scoped, especially in sequential editing tasks. articles.title: Learning Dynamic Games for Cooperative Iterative Tasks
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28901v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We consider cooperative and iterative tasks involving multiple agents whose interactions are modeled as a dynamic game with shared constraints. We propose a general learning framework applicable to nonlinear and nonconvex dynamic games that uses previously executed feasible trajectories to construct a sampled joint safe set and player-specific cost-to-go functions. At each time step, the agents jointly select a previously sampled terminal state and a Generalized Nash equilibrium used to reach it. A new solution is adopted only if it satisfies a cooperative acceptance rule agreed upon by the players. The framework accommodates individual non-degradation requirements and selection criteria such as weighted costs and Nash bargaining. We show that the proposed framework guarantees recursive feasibility and characterize conditions under which each player's cost is non-increasing across iterations.

This system integrates perceptual context with planned future trajectories to generate natural-language explanations of robot movement. We deploy the system on a Unitree Go2 platform in indoor navigation scenarios and evaluate how different explanation context configurations affect user trust and explanation satisfaction. Abstract: Modern robotic agents are increasingly expected to support steerable control, where a single policy can adjust its behavioral style at runtime under changing user preferences. Preference-conditioned reinforcement learning provides this interface, but conditioning alone does not ensure that a requested behavior change is strong, does not leak into unrelated behaviors, and does not compromise task performance. We use these measures to compare reward-level, advantage-level, loss-level, and PCGrad-based aggregation across two humanoid-control frameworks. Abstract: Safe robotic task planning requires planners that can reliably achieve task goals while satisfying safety constraints. Classical planners search over explicit symbolic task representations and can provide formal guarantees with respect to encoded safety constraints, but require rigid input formats. In contrast, large language models (LLMs) offer flexible task interfaces and strong generalization capabilities, but they are large, power-hungry, and pre-trained with little robot-specific safety data and knowledge. articles.title: 具身记忆赛道持续升温，长记忆迎来新 SOTA
articles.content: IROS 2026 最佳论文启示录：没有长记忆的机器人，终将被淘汰。    作者丨邓哲敏    编辑丨齐铖湧                                                                                                       本月初在匹兹堡闭幕的 IROS 2026 将最佳论文奖颁给了 LT-Mem，这项研究让机器人重访同一空间时，能完整保留每个物体的位置变迁史，而非仅仅记住最新一次看到的样子。评委会从近两千篇收录论文中选中它，想必不仅是认可其扎实的工作，也是代表学界宣告：具身长记忆（long-term embodied memory）已经从一个工程补丁，变成了机器人领域公认的科学问题。从实际角度考虑，通用机器人要规模化落地，需要以小时、天乃至周为单位持续运行，而不只是几分钟。没有长记忆，每次相遇都是初次见面，机器人只是一个个孤立的单次动作执行器；有了长记忆，它才能从一次性工具变成可以长期上岗的同事。但解决这件事远不是扩大上下文窗口那么简单：持续涌入的多模态数据既无法全部存储，也无法全部检索；现实世界还在不断变化，新的观察既不能简单覆盖旧的，也不能无序堆叠；更棘手的是，一条错误的记忆会在之后的决策里被反复调用，错误由此层层放大。记忆如何写入、如何留证、如何纠错，都是需要被正面回答的问题，靠调几个工程参数解决不了。AI科技评论（雷峰网公众号）注意到，在这一方向被顶会加冕的数月前，国内具身初创公司贝塔无限就已坐上牌桌。今年五月，贝塔的联合创始人陶帅在采访中明确表示：长效、多模态、时空记忆的缺失，是他们首先要重点突破的方向。随后，团队陆续发布 BetaMem 全时空多模态记忆架构、世界动作模型 BetaWAM 0.1、首款机器人多米。10 月 20 日，团队把 BetaMem 的写入学习、证据管理和自我改进机制写成了系统的方法与实验，挂上 arXiv。论文交出的成绩单颇为亮眼：BetaMem 采用 9B 开源模型生成记忆，在 M3-Bench-robot、LoCoMo、OpenEQA 和 EgoLifeQA 四项代表性记忆基准的对比评测中均取得 SOTA 成绩。尤其在串联多次观察中的线索、回忆长时间跨度的事件、识别个人习惯等任务上，BetaMem 展现出明显优势——这些能力，正是机器人进入生活、持续积累对人与环境的了解所需要的。LT-Mem 从多会话建图切入，把问题收窄到干净、可评测；BetaMem 则从记忆如何形成、如何验证、如何从失败中学习的系统视角，搭建完整的记忆底座。一边是顶尖学术单点攻坚摘得顶会桂冠，一边是国内团队以产业落地为目标搭建完整记忆底座，学术和产业在此交汇，足以证明长记忆是整个领域正在收敛的核心方向判断。01记忆这道题，学界做到哪一步围绕机器人长期记忆，学界探索了许多方法。按年份罗列意义不大，AI科技评论（雷峰网公众号）想换个角度，看记忆回答了什么问题，还剩什么没回答。第一类关注空间侧的记忆，也就是“这里有什么”。Hydra、ConceptGraphs 等三维场景图把物体、地点、房间组织成可被语言查询的关系网，Khronos 把时间引入动态环境建图，DynaMem 让移动操作机器人在物体被挪动后继续更新记忆，真机上对非静止物体的取放成功率平均达 70%，是静态系统的两倍以上。这一支空间关系清楚，但记住的主要是当下这一版世界长什么样。第二类关注检测类的记忆，也就是“我见过什么”。ReMEmbR 把长时导航视频建成可检索的时空记忆，供智能体推理。但检索按相似度排序，取回的是过去的信息。五分钟前桌上确实有杯子，现在还在不在呢？检索不负责回答。第三类关注变化侧的记忆，也就是“它变了没有”。LT-Mem 正是这一思路。论文把现有系统的毛病命名为“时间性失忆”：要么用新观测覆盖旧状态，要么存下语义快照却没有跨次访问一致的物体身份。它用一个随物体习性变化的易变性分数，决定新观察该覆盖、保持还是并存。作者也坦承局限：测试只覆盖两个室内加一个室外场景、各 10 次访问，外观相似物体的身

articles.title: Agentic World Action Models
articles.content: Recent world action models provide visual foresight and future prediction for robot manipulation, but lack explicit mechanisms for compositional skill reuse. Agentic robotics combines code-based planning and reasoning with reusable skills, but often lacks predictive grounding in physical dynamics. We introduce AW-0, an agentic world action model framework that integrates code-based planning with joint video and action prediction. We jointly model code, future video, and robot actions as three coupled generative streams within a unified mixture-of-transformers architecture. Within this architecture a code expert generates parameterized skill routines and control logic while video and action experts generate future visual states and low-level motor commands. Code serves two complementary roles: it structures multi-step prediction and control within the world model and represents skills as reusable programs for subsequent agentic execution. We further introduce an automated curation pipeline that labels robot and human video trajectories with aligned programs and consolidates recurring routines into reusable skill libraries. Evaluations on RoboTwin 2.0 and physical bimanual manipulation tasks show improved task performance over VLA and WAM baselines, alongside gains in language following, semantic reasoning and robustness, demonstrating that agentic code enables connection between planning, prediction and execution within WAMs.

articles.title: LongZero: Enhancing Long-Context Reasoning in LLMs from Zero Data
articles.content: Reinforcement learning (RL) is an effective way to strengthen the long-context reasoning of large language models (LLMs), but it needs training data that are long, diverse, challenging, and verifiable. Human annotation of such data is expensive, naturally occurring data are too scarce to sustain RL, and existing synthesis methods depend on external corpora or stronger teacher models, which become harder to obtain as the trained models get stronger. Recently, RL from zero data, in which a model learns from tasks it proposes itself, has achieved excellent performance, but existing methods target short-context tasks. Therefore, we propose $\textbf{LongZero}$, a method that lets an LLM improve its own long-context reasoning without any external data. Instead of writing questions and answers over existing documents, LongZero first has the model synthesize the question and answer with its supporting evidence in a compact structured form, and only then separately expands the evidence into a long multi-document context. LongZero combines these self-written multi-hop reasoning tasks with self-written multi-round retrieval tasks and trains the model with GRPO. We evaluate LongZero on two LLMs across five long-context reasoning benchmarks and compare it with RL on data synthesized from external corpora. Experimental results show that LongZero can generalize to real tasks, and outperforms both baselines, suggesting a viable and promising path to improving long-context reasoning of LLMs.

articles.title: Rethinking Video Autoencoders for Interactive World Models
articles.content: Video world models predict future frames from past frames and actions. They serve as simulators in which agents train, plan or are evaluated, and that humans can control interactively. They generate in the latent space of a video autoencoder, whose compression sets their cost per frame and how long each action waits to take effect. Yet world models often reuse the autoencoders of text-to-video generators, built for offline generation with no agent waiting and, without their training data and code, not retrainable at another compression. We therefore ask how, where and how much a world model should compress. We build CADRE, an open family of causal diffusion representation autoencoders spanning multiple spatio-temporal compressions. Its members differ only in a small bottleneck on frozen features and share a diffusion decoder self-distilled to one or a few steps. We train the same world model on each autoencoder in two domains, manipulation and navigation, with two environments each. CADRE forms most of the latency-quality frontier, especially with a moving camera. Our study also leads to four findings. At strong compression, a diffusion decoder is sharper than perceptual regression. In robot manipulation, temporal compression is more effective in the autoencoder than in the world model. Manipulation and navigation call for opposite compressions: temporal compression costs little when the camera is still, and spatial compression when it moves. Surprisingly, with a still camera, coarser spatial tokens hurt motion far more than image quality. Code, models and a live demo are at https://kyutai.org/blog/2026-10-21-cadre

articles.title: Think Harder Where It Matters: Item-Level Adaptive Recursion for Sequential Recommendation
articles.content: Existing sequential recommenders usually allocate a fixed computational budget to every item in a user's interaction history, regardless of the item's contribution to the final prediction. We challenge this de facto design with two diagnostic findings. (1) Non-uniform computational need: items within the same sequence vary drastically in how much computation they require. Most converge after shallow processing while a critical minority only stabilizes at full depth. (2) Suboptimality of fixed allocation: given oracle access to the target item, a non-uniform depth assignment consistently outranks the fixed one, indicating that existing uniform computation both wastes capacity on already-converged items and sacrifices overall recommendation quality. These observations motivate a shift from fixed-depth computation to item-level adaptive reasoning. To this end, we propose LoopRec. LoopRec recursively applies a single weight-shared block and introduces a lightweight gate at each recursion boundary that makes a binary exit-or-continue decision for every item independently. Items whose representations have sufficiently matured exit early, while those requiring deeper reasoning continue to subsequent recursions. This design converts the fixed global depth into a learned, per-item property without auxiliary depth labels, and is readily adaptable to diverse backbone architectures. Extensive experiments on public benchmarks with four backbone families demonstrate that LoopRec consistently outperforms matched fixed-depth counterparts. Further analysis reveals that LoopRec's learned allocation exhibits interpretable patterns aligned with our post-hoc oracle analysis: lower-frequency items and more recent interactions naturally receive deeper computation. Our code is available at https://github.com/Elpmis117/LoopRec.

articles.title: VoxProg: 3D Spatial Reasoning through Voxel Programming
articles.content: Language models' abilities to interpret tasks and generate programs offer a promising basis for 3D spatial reasoning. Yet following spatial instructions in 3D scenes requires programs to construct geometric references that language leaves implicit. In this work, we introduce VoxProg, which formulates 3D object placement through voxel programming: a language model translates task interpretations into executable programs over local voxel views of scene surfaces. Because these views index surface geometry on regular grids with explicit coordinates and neighborhood relations, an evidence program can isolate task-relevant regions and boundaries directly from scene meshes, and a downstream pose program can measure the resulting geometry to compute a target $SE(3)$ pose. Visual and numerical feedback from execution lets the model inspect intermediate selections and candidate placements to iteratively revise its code. To evaluate open-ended placement across functional use, geometric fit, and contextual arrangements, we introduce the 71-task VoxProg-Bench benchmark along with an evaluation suite pairing perceptual Intent Alignment and 3D Physical Validity. Across VoxProg-Bench and external benchmarks, VoxProg consistently outperforms relation-based, keypoint-based, and mesh-based baselines.

articles.title: PhysiCalWorld: In-Context Physics Calibration for World Models
articles.content: Existing world models typically perceive a scene through current visual frame or a narrow history window. However, these observations may not reveal the physics properties that determine transition dynamics, such as an object's mass distribution, joint damping, or surface friction. Without calibrating these physics factors for world models, predictions tend to regress toward an empirical prior and induce severe drift in novel test scenes. To this end, we propose PhysiCalWorld, which calibrates action-conditioned world models to the instance-specific dynamics via in-context prompting, without fine-tuning or analytical physics modeling. Our method encodes an exploratory interaction clip collected within the test scene into a compact physics descriptor token, which grounds subsequent predictions in the scene's actual physical behavior. PhysiCalWorld is trained end-to-end with the latent prediction loss alone, without physics labels. At inference time, the descriptor token is extracted once and can be reused across rollouts with negligible compute overhead. We evaluate PhysiCalWorld across four environments covering diverse physics variations and show that it substantially improves rollout prediction accuracy and visual planning success rate. The learned descriptors also form a physically structured latent space and generalize beyond the physics ranges seen during training.

articles.content: We give an algorithm for computing an $\eps$-approximate fixed point of any $d$-dimensional nonexpansion with respect to the $\ell_\infty$ norm in time $\log(1/\eps)^{O(\log^2 d)}$. Among other consequences, our algorithm implies that simple stochastic games can be solved in quasipolynomial time.

articles.title: ALPS: Visual State Encoders for World Models
articles.content: World models turn visual representations into predictions and actions. We argue that their visual foundation should combine physical-state information, native language alignment, and pixel reconstruction, so that a single representation can support prediction, instruction, and inspection. However, existing encoders typically specialize in only one or two of these capabilities; we therefore introduce ALPS, a pretrained visual state encoder that unifies all three in a single set of patch tokens. Using only still images and text, we pretrain a ViT-B/16 from scratch with language, reconstruction, and spatial correspondence objectives, and then refine it via cross-view self-distillation. In a unified evaluation across fifteen public encoders, ALPS achieves the lowest aggregate LIBERO state-probe error among ViT-B models (matching the 3.5x larger V-JEPA 2-L) while maintaining strong language alignment and accurate pixel reconstruction. Downstream, frozen ALPS tokens reach the highest mean policy success on LIBERO (85.5%) when paired with our native text tower, match or exceed leading encoders on world-model planning across PushT, Wall, and Granular, and allow predicted future tokens to be decoded directly into pixels for visual inspection. We hope this work helps establish visual pretraining as a shared foundation for understanding, prediction, and action in world models.

articles.title: Self-normalized Bernstein Inequalities for Regenerative Processes and Applications to Learning Without Independence
articles.content: We prove a self-normalized Bernstein inequality for bounded functions of a regenerative process with independent, identically distributed marked cycles of finite mean length. The bound uses observed cycle lengths and retains explicit terms for truncation and the cycle ending after the observation horizon. Selecting a tuning parameter from a finite deterministic collection gives a version of Bernstein inequality where all terms are empirical but one, related to the tails of the regeneration times. We then study this term in many regimes: it turns out that it is of second-order in many cases of interest. This is important for applications in machine learning: we prove generalization error bounds for classification with non-i.i.d., regenerative data. These bounds can be used to define learning objectives: by minimizing the first-order term only in the bound, we define agnostic classifiers that still satisfy oracle inequalities. We also show that the bound on the average deviation provided by our results is minimax-optimal in the sample size and in the expected regeneration time. Finally, we combine the Bernstein inequality with a regenerative strong approximation to obtain a Gaussian approximation using an observable block variance estimator.

articles.title: The role of locality and weight sharing in convolutional neural networks
articles.content: The success of convolutional neural networks is often attributed to locality and weight sharing. However, how these two properties separately shape learning, and how their effects depend on the spatial correlations of natural images, remain poorly understood. We address these questions in a teacher-student model with a convolutional teacher acting on $P$ input positions with correlation $c$ between positions. We compare convolutional and locally connected students trained by online stochastic gradient descent, and derive ordinary differential equations that describe their dynamics exactly in the limit of large feature dimension $D$. For uncorrelated positions ($c = 0$), the two students follow the same learning trajectory, with the convolutional student learning exactly $P$ times faster. We also find that locality affects the sample complexity: a student that matches the kernel size of the teacher recovers it from $\mathcal{O}_{D}(D)$ samples, whereas $\mathcal{O}_{D}(D\log(D))$ samples are needed with a larger kernel. For $c > 0$, spatial correlations can reduce the advantage of weight sharing. The asymptotic error of the convolutional student grows with $c$, whereas that of the locally connected student is independent of $c$ and overall lower when evaluated at the same learning rate. When the learning rate is instead tuned to the training horizon, however, the locally connected student wins at early times and the convolutional student at late times, with a transition that we predict analytically.

articles.title: CW-WAM: A Structured Contact-Wrench World Action Model for Force-Sensitive Manipulation
articles.content: Force-sensitive manipulation requires contact and load information that is not provided explicitly by visual observations. We present CW-WAM, a world action model that jointly predicts video, motion, and contact wrench. Inspired by hybrid motion-force control, it contains a unified interaction module that treats both motion and contact wrench as modeling targets and predicts time-aligned motion-wrench chunks as control references. A pair-causal attention mechanism structures the motion-wrench dependencies, while a long fixed-length wrench memory retains past interaction information. The predicted wrench chunk acts as a force reference for a 20-Hz outer-loop admittance controller within a slow-fast control system that maintains force feedback and smooth motion between model queries. CW-WAM improves contact prediction and increases the insertion success rate from 25% to 70% for square pegs with 1-mm clearance per side and from 40% to 95% for power adapters, compared with WAM without wrench input. It also improves lifting-height accuracy across different loads. Our framework with an admittance controller reduces force-reference RMSE from 4.8 to 2.7 N for peg insertion and from 2.0 to 1.3 N for wiping, respectively, with smaller force fluctuations during successful execution. Project website: https://cw-wam-project.github.io/

articles.title: Environment Duels: A Microcosm of LLM Co-Evolution
articles.content: Through a tangle of real-world interactions, from synthetic training pipelines to data shared on the open web, frontier LLMs absorb what their predecessors and competitors create. How well does each model play its role in this ecosystem, as a creator and as a solver? We introduce Environment Duels, a dynamic agentic benchmark that evaluates both capabilities on interactive environments. Each model writes environments, each with a privileged hint, aiming for tasks that capable solvers fail without the hint and pass with it. Across nine frontier LLMs, solving and authoring prove to be distinct skills: the strongest solvers are not the strongest authors, while smaller models learn more from how others played and write the hardest environments and the most useful hints. Beyond the scores, the pairwise interactions form a microcosm of how models affect one another. Head-to-head outcomes are transitive and so yield a stable ranking; independent authors converge on the same designs; and in a reinforcement-learning study with Qwen3.8-27B, the learner's hint lift on an author's environments tracks how much training on those environments improves it on held-out reasoning and agentic benchmarks, whether the environments are its own or another model's. Each of these patterns has a counterpart in how models shape one another outside the duel. By staging these interactions under controlled conditions, Environment Duels offers a window onto how LLMs teach, challenge and learn from one another. Code is available at https://github.com/LLM-Duels/EnvDuels.

articles.title: The End of Consensus Research?
articles.content: Consensus is a fundamental problem in distributed computing and at the core of state machine replication (SMR). Despite decades of active human research, discovering practical low-latency solutions to the problem is still open, as it requires combining protocol knowledge, correctness reasoning, implementation, and experimental evaluation. We report on how AI helped us discover A-greement, a new consensus protocol for geo-replicated state machines that significantly outperforms state-of-the-art solutions. Averaged across six deployments with 5 or 9 replicas, A-greement reduces the mean latency of a geo-distributed key-value store over the fastest baseline by 12.2% and 33.3% on write-heavy and read-heavy workloads, respectively, and matches the fastest baseline on read-only workloads. A-greement combines lease-authorized local reads, direct client learning for leader-ordered writes, and a fast fixed-quorum per-key write path, selected according to network topology and workload. At the heart of our discovery lies AI-greement, an agent harness for the "autonomous" discovery, implementation, experimentation, and verification of candidate protocols. AI-greement integrates (1) a concept-oriented protocol knowledge base, (2) a modular implementation skeleton, and (3) a Lean-based verification framework with reusable safety definitions, reference specifications, and proofs. AI-greement is of independent interest: its Lean formalization uncovers several previously unreported vulnerabilities in existing consensus protocols, and it provides guidelines on how domain-specific harnesses can turn general-purpose coding agents into effective tools for (distributed) computing research. Yet we argue that human consensus experts remain essential before, during, and after the search: agents reshape the researcher's role rather than end consensus research.

articles.title: Quant-Arena: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Quantitative Trading Research
articles.content: Quantitative research is an iterative loop: a researcher proposes a market hypothesis, implements it as an executable signal, tests it on historical data, and decides what to keep. Existing benchmarks score formulas, code, or individual trading decisions, leaving open whether large language models (LLMs) can complete this loop and produce strategies that work beyond the research period. We introduce Quant-Arena, a benchmark and public leaderboard for end-to-end quantitative research on real A-share market data. A model constructs features and stock-scoring code, receives feedback only on 2022--2023, and freezes one strategy for assessment on the sealed year 2024. A cash-account evaluator applies trading constraints and costs, including market impact estimated from a simulated order book. Scores are dominated by realized excess return and complemented by signal quality and the diversity of features used by the strategy. We evaluate nine frontier models, among which GPT-6 Astra scores highest; yet no model beats the equal-weight market in 2024. Quant-Arena is open to submissions from any model or agent harness.

articles.title: Minimax Optimality of the NPMLE for Gaussian Mixtures in Hellinger Distance
articles.content: We analyze the problem of estimating univariate Gaussian mixture densities using the nonparametric maximum likelihood estimator (NPMLE) based on $n$ independent and identically distributed samples. We show that the unconstrained NPMLE achieves the minimax optimal rate $\log(n)/n$ in squared Hellinger distance, when the true mixing measure is sub-Gaussian. In addition, we show that when the true mixing measure has compact support, the NMPLE constrained to a compact interval also achieves the minimax optimal rate, which is slightly faster and of order $\log(n)/(n \log \log n)$. Our proof consists of sharply characterizing the local Hellinger bracketing entropy of the class of finite Gaussian mixtures. One of our key technical innovations is to sharply bound the $L^2$ bracketing entropy of balls of bounded-degree polynomials, which may be of independent interest. As an application, we establish the regret-optimality of $g$-modeling procedures based on the NPMLE in the Gaussian Empirical Bayes problem with bounded priors.

articles.title: Multimodal Embodied Agents: A Unified Capability-centric Perspective from Computer-Use to Robot-Use
articles.content: Multimodal agents (MMAs) sustain interaction through reasoning, memory, tools, and feedback, most visibly as computer-use agents, while robotic systems (RSs) couple sensing and actuation under physical dynamics. We define multimodal embodied agents (MMEAs) as goal-directed systems that couple multimodal task reasoning with physical action and revise decisions from the resulting feedback. This raises a central question: what changes when a multimodal agent moves from computer-use to robot-use? We introduce PAPAV, a unified capability-centric framework of five recurring functions: Perceive the current state, Anticipate action effects, Plan a feasible course, Act through an interface or body, and Verify the outcome. Defined by function rather than architecture, these capabilities let PAPAV identify what all three share and then compare MMEAs with MMAs and with RSs. Five physical constraints, from partial observability to unverifiable outcomes, leave fewer choices fixed in advance and less room to reverse errors. Across 64 benchmarks, explicit evaluation centers on Act; only 5 assess Anticipate and 3 assess Verify, leaving both largely hidden behind task success. These constraints also frame the open challenges we identify. PAPAV therefore provides a common basis for designing reliable physical agents and measuring progress across all five capabilities rather than task success alone.

articles.title: Velocity Ambiguity Profiles: Time-Resolved Bayes-Risk Diagnostics for Flow Matching
articles.content: Flow matching trains a continuum of velocity regression problems but usually reports a loss averaged over interpolation time, obscuring which regions are limited by intrinsic ambiguity and which remain data-limited. We introduce the Velocity Ambiguity Profile (VAP), $\mathcal{A}_v(t)$, the time-local Bayes-risk floor of velocity prediction, and decompose time-resolved loss as $L_N(t)=\mathcal{A}_v(t)+R(t;N)$, where only the excess term $R(t;N)$ is reducible by more data or a different estimator. For $N$ training samples and a $K$-component mixture in the structured example, we prove two statistical benchmarks. In an intrinsic local-regression benchmark, $\mathcal{A}_v(t)$ enters the time-dependent noise factor of the standard nonparametric rate. In separated isotropic Gaussian mixtures, the Bayes velocity becomes locally affine, and a label-oracle residual-regression benchmark has parametric excess-risk scale $K\mathcal{A}_v(t)/N$, matched within the same separated residual Gaussian-location subproblem. Controlled Gaussian-mixture experiments validate this diagnostic through a dense transition sweep, calibrated oracle-to-blind and empirical-proxy audits, and a local controlled time-sampler stress test in which a frozen reducible-error proxy reduces reducible loss while cross-cell sensitivity delimits aggressive sampling. On CIFAR-100 DINOv2 feature flow, guided time sampling reduces uniformly evaluated velocity loss by $6.78\%$ and global feature Fréchet distance (FD) by $23.6\%$, while class-conditional kernel inception distance (KID) shows no improvement. VAP turns an averaged flow-matching objective into a time-resolved diagnostic for locating ambiguity-limited and data-limited regions.

articles.title: Asymmetric On-Policy Distillation Learns In-Context Exploration
articles.content: Sequential decision-making under partial observability is difficult because agents must explore to infer hidden, task-relevant information before acting effectively. Learning such information-gathering behaviors tabula rasa via online reinforcement learning is sample-inefficient, whereas offline imitation averages expert actions across hidden states and fails to learn exploration. In this work, we propose ASTEROID, a simple and effective student--teacher supervised learning framework that can learn test-time exploration. Although a privileged expert never needs to explore, we demonstrate that a history-conditioned student can learn to do so when trained with on-policy contexts: the student first collects on-policy context under partial observability, and the privileged expert provides action labels conditioned on that context. By distilling expert actions directly conditioned on the student's on-policy history, the student learns to systematically resolve partial observability, i.e., search while uncertain and exploit once the hidden state is revealed. This enables efficient test-time exploration (similar to Bayesian posterior sampling) without incurring the impractical training-data costs of reinforcement learning. Across a diverse range of eleven different environments, including discrete exploration benchmarks, robotic manipulation, navigation, and Procgen environments, ASTEROID achieves ~2x higher returns under fixed exploration budgets, uses ~100x fewer interactions than RL baselines, and outperforms frontier models at exploration. Finally, our method transfers policies trained in simulation to vision-denied real-world robot manipulation, exhibiting efficient exploration and increasing success by +40% over standard distillation. Overall, it provides a simple yet surprisingly effective framework to learn efficient test-time exploration.

articles.title: BatchBench: Benchmarking AI Robustness to Batch Effects and Domain Shift in Biomedical Images - A JUMP Cell Painting Leaderboard
articles.content: Despite recent advances, current AI systems remain highly susceptible to domain shifts, particularly in biomedical imaging, where images are usually acquired under substantially different experimental conditions. Although recent domain adaptation methods have made substantial progress, significant performance gaps under domain shift persist. To measure progress in this regard, we introduce BatchBench, a leaderboard that evaluates and compares the robustness of AI systems on biomedical images from unseen experimental batches and data sources. BatchBench is built on JUMP-CP, one of the largest publicly available biomedical imaging datasets. Generated using the Cell Painting assay, JUMP-CP exhibits pronounced batch effects and domain shifts, making it a challenging testbed for evaluating robustness to distributional changes.
